quest.title: The Mysterious Letter
quest.description: You and Paimon return to Sumeru to visit some local friends.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Mora x31125, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

talks.objective: Return to Sumeru and take a look

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Do you see him? The old man flailing around.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Is he the one you wanted to talk to about the case?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Correct. His name is Cyrus, a former Spantamad Sage. He taught both me and Lisa.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? Cyno's teacher is in trouble?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: It's ridiculous... I'm just an old man who enjoys a spot of gardening, shopping, and wine. What sort of person targets an old retiree?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Professor, I've brought some friends.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Ah, Cyno! Now, who do we have here...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Hmm? Hold on, let me think... A flying fairy dressed in white, a youth who does not seem to hail from this land.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: My goodness, you must be the legendary Traveler and Paimon. I've heard all about what you've done for Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! Looks like we're really famous!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I've told him about you before. You are my friends, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good to meet you, Sir. We're here to help Cyno.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That's right. Let me summarize the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: A couple of days ago, Professor Cyrus suddenly received a threat letter.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A threat letter!?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Exactly! Who sends a threat letter to an old man like me, for goodness' sake?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: This is the letter in question.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Cyrus, I have uncovered your secret. If you wish to prevent it from going public, leave ten million Mora at the back door of the café."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Secondly, don't come looking for me. You'll never find me, but I will always be watching you and all of your secrets. Finally, if you dare to report this to the matra, there will be consequences."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow. They sure didn't mince their words...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Clearly, this person must be desperate for Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Ten million Mora! What a joke!

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: I'm just a single retiree, with nothing to my name beyond the tomatoes in my garden... Where do people think I'm hiding ten million Mora, hmm? In my tomatoes?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: #There were no witnesses, so currently the letter is all we've got. So {NICKNAME}, Paimon, let's put our heads together.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ready when you are.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's ready, too!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Alright, take a look. Do you see anything suspicious?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (From Cyno's description, it sounds like the threat letter didn't come in an envelope. It was simply written on a crude piece of paper, and left for Cyrus to find.)

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Very good. The paper has a rather rough texture. It's not the typical kind you see in most books.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Another thing is, some of these strokes look kinda blurry... Could there be an issue with the ink?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Possibly. And I bet the paper has something to do with it.

response.speaker: Cyrus
response.text: Most of the paper around here is much smoother than this, and the ink is absorbed quickly so it doesn't run. This paper, meanwhile... It's very coarse grained. Almost as if it's... made from some sort of plant matter?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: It's certainly not the same paper as we use in the Akademiya. But the ink is nothing special. Just regular black ink, that gets a blue tinge when applied to paper.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... So do we think the culprit has a connection with the Akademiya, or not?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait! Check this out. Looks like this part got wet at some point.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Agreed. The staining suggests it was a colored liquid, not plain water. It also looks like it was wiped off with a damp cloth.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A colored liquid? So... tea? Wine?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Looks like we're thinking along similar lines. Let's go talk to Aarav — there are some things I'll need him to take care of.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Yes. Some of the strokes are blurry.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So is there something wrong with the ink?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Possibly. And I bet the paper has something to do with it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woah, the Akademiya sure is busy during the day!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... But where should we go looking for people that we know...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cyno! It's been so long since we last saw you!

choices.text: Really feels like it's been forever.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Welcome back to Sumeru City. I'm delighted to meet you again.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: So. What brings you back here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, nothing in particular. Paimon just... saw a really big mushroom out on the road the other day, and suddenly missed all our friends in Sumeru.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Funnily enough, we were reminiscing about you recently, too. It was at a group dinner. I look forward to hearing about your travels — something tells me we must have a lot to catch up on.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really, you were thinking of us too? What a coincidence!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Indeed... Or as I call it, the Biryani factor.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: ...You really want me to say the rest? Heh, okay. It's always rice to meat stew again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... darn, he said it!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I win the bet, Paimon! Time to pay up.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: You like that one, huh? You must, if you remember it after all this time. Admit the truth! You have long been in awe of my razor-sharp wit.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, alright, here's your five hundred Mora...

choices.text: Thanks, Cyno. Feels good to hit the jackpot.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: You're exaggerating. It's only five hundred Mora.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, five hundred Mora is still a lot of snacks to Paimon!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Alright, I'll treat you to some desserts later.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Anyway, I'm actually investigating a case right now. My mind is focused on work, which is why I didn't complete the joke at first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A case? What happened?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Nothing major. But after finding out who was involved, I decided, on reflection, to handle this one myself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Need any help? We only came here to hang out, so we've got the time. You may as well take us with you, and then when you're done, we can, uh... y'know! *nom* *nom*

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Such enthusiasm. Are you worried I'll forget about treating you to some sweets if you're not around to remind me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whaaat? Nooo! ...Alright, was it really that obvious?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Obvious enough. Still, it's a fine idea. You are the heroes of Sumeru. It makes perfect sense to work together.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Alright. Follow me.

choices.text: Thanks, Paimon. Feels good to hit the jackpot.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's never making a bet again... Paimon really thought Cyno would be able to hold back on the jokes... They say people can change, but maybe that's just wishful thinking.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Ah, so this was technically my fault? In that case, I'll treat you to some sweets later.

choices.text: You look like you've been keeping well.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: As do you. You don't seem weary at all from your travels — if anything, you seem stronger.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Aarav, Aarav... Ah, there he is.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: #Mahamatra Cyno, Sir Cyrus. Ah, and {NICKNAME} and Paimon. It's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Cyno briefs Aarav on the case...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...As such, I'm inclined to believe that the culprit in this case is a student at the Akademiya. Somebody young, and strapped for cash.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Oh, one last thing. I'd start your investigation by taking a look at the cafes in the city.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, of course! You think the culprit spilled their coffee on the letter, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: They do look like coffee stains to me.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Also, if I'm not mistaken, the letter is written on a type of scented paper that has aromatics added during the manufacturing process. The kind often provided as writing material for customers in cafes and taverns.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Ahh, of course... Yes, like they sell in the gift shops. I remember now, Zaha Hadi bought some a while back. She said she was going to use it as wrapping paper for a vase.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: Understood. I'll assemble a team to investigate the points of interest immediately.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: You have my gratitude.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: One last thing: Send some matra to guard the entrances and exits of Sumeru City. And change into plain clothes — don't let them see you coming.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: Will do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great thinking, Cyno! So... Where do we think the culprit's at right now?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I doubt they'd go back to the cafe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah... They've probably been lying low at home, waiting to see how Cyrus reacts...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hm, you're right, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Which part?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The culprit's approach.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Whatever happens, they need this Mora. But just because they warned Professor Cyrus not to go to the matra doesn't mean they know what he'll do next. So like you said, they need to wait and see.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: And crucially, the culprit said they'd be watching the professor's every move.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait, are you saying...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eek!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Found you.
Argh! Wh—What are you doing!?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You wrote the threat letter.
I—I don't know what you're talking about! What threat letter?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I sensed someone was watching us from the shadows the moment we entered the House of Daena. You managed to stay relatively well hidden for someone reckless enough to threaten Professor Cyrus.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: There are a lot of people here, but we were looking specifically for Aarav. Whoever followed us the whole way was likely to be the culprit.
I—I was just listening in, that's all! ...You know something big's going down when Mahamatra Cyno shows up! Right? So I got a little curious, what's the big deal?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: You smiled when Aarav left. I saw it as clear as day.
Is smiling a crime now!?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: There are coffee stains on the letter. You mixed some coffee with water, gently smeared it onto the paper, then wiped it off with a wet cloth. All to create the impression that the letter was written at a cafe.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Closing off the exits to the city doesn't affect you, because you already live here. And as long as the matra were focused on the cafes, you would be free from scrutiny.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The cafe was a red herring all along. You had to be somewhere where you could monitor the professor's movements.
You can't pin this on me! I haven't done anything!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Really? Then why are you shaking like a leaf?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The innocent have no reason to fear the matra. But you...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Your heart's racing, and your eyelids are twitching. You're a terrible liar.
...I would never—

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Don't try anything, or you'll pay the price. Now, come with me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that was over quickly. Cyno already caught the guy...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: You're telling me! One minute I go out for a quick smoke, the next minute I see Aarav, already on his way back to meet up with Cyno.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: *sigh*... Looked like a young guy, too. Couldn't have been much more than thirty. But after what he's done, I'm afraid he's ruined his whole future.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Everyone, it's all over.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gosh, that was so fast!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The culprit's name is Urraca. A sixteen-year-old student in the Rtawahist Darshan.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sixteen!? Cyrus thought he looked thirty-something...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: We checked his records. He's sixteen. A third-year student.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: But... he looks so old...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, seriously!

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: *sigh* Foolish child... He's too young for the criminal life. What the devil drove him down this path?

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: We questioned the culprit regarding his motives. He, umm...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Oh, just spit it out. Nothing can surprise me at this point.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: Very well. It's our understanding that Urraca is a mediocre student who has been underperforming in his classes. He started taking extra tutoring to improve his grades, but developed a gambling habit around the same time and lost a lot of Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: Down on his luck, he went to the tavern for a drink, and overheard some people chatting about Sir Cyrus's comfortable retirement. They mentioned that he's always arguing about his tomato plants with some old woman on the street...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: "Some old woman on the street"? Goodness gracious, has that rascal attended a single one of his classes? That "old woman" is Kshahrewar's very own Professor Zaha Hadi! How can he not know who Zaha Hadi is?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...Is this going somewhere?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Oh! Right, yes, umm... So another thing — we don't just argue about tomato plants... And what are they trying to insinuate by "comfortable retirement"? A man grows a few vegetables, and suddenly he's living a life of luxury?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Maybe it's more the fact that you have the time to grow vegetables in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: Urraca mentioned he'd heard a rumor, alleging that Sir Cyrus illegally obtained a large sum of money from the desert before retiring, and kept it for himself instead of reporting it to the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: Urraca believes this money to be the reason why Sir Cyrus hasn't kept up with any academic research or other projects since his retirement... And given your advanced age, he thought that you'd be an easy target to blackmail.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Oh, Urraca... I'm at a loss for words. I'm so angry I don't know where to start!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: People make up rumors all the time. I am quite confident that Professor Cyrus has never embezzled a Mora in his life.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Aarav, you'll have to find an excuse to interrogate Urraca again later. I need you to deliver a few firm fistfuls to him on my behalf.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: I completely understand how you feel, Sir Cyrus. But I'm afraid that course of action goes against the matra's principles.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Professor, there's no need to be childish about this.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Oh come on, I was clearly joking.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, okay... Where does this go from here?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The Akademiya will determine the appropriate disciplinary action against the student. And as for the individuals spreading rumors about the professor's obsession with tomatoes and some old woman on the street... There could be a slander case here. The matra will continue to investigate.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Who said I'm obsessed with some old woman on the street!? Mind your wording, or you'll start a whole new rumor!

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: ...You seem confused. Haha, don't you understand?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Urraca is just a young boy who made a very rash and very stupid decision based on some groundless rumor he heard. Besides, I didn't actually hand over any Mora to him. The whole thing sounds a lot worse than it is.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: All it's cost me is a little reputational damage, that's all.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Please rest assured, Professor, that the Akademiya will issue a fair and reasonable punishment.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Yes, I have no doubt about that.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: But as a former educator, I'd still like to have a serious conversation with the boy's parents. The family lives in the city, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Correct.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: We looked into the family. Both parents are merchants, and they're often away on business. They've never taken much of an active role in their children's lives.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: *sigh* What a mess...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: You don't have to seal the evidence away yet, do you? I'd like to have that letter back for the time being, if possible. I'll need something concrete for when I talk to the family tonight.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: We have to show them how serious this situation is!

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: The relevant authorities have already reviewed the evidence and are now discussing Urraca's punishment. You can hold onto the letter for now — just make sure to return it within a couple of days.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Oh! So you'll be able to close the case in two days?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Give or take. Cases like this are quick to resolve.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Very good. Well, thank you all for your help — perhaps we can all go for a meal together? My treat, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Aarav
dialogues.text: My apologies, Sir Cyrus, but I have a prior commitment. Enjoy the meal, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Ah, I see... well, that's a pity. But Cyno, you have to come. You found the culprit at record speed, and I owe you for that.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Ah — and isn't Tighnari in town at the moment? Bring him along too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you mean Tighnari's in the city?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: He is. Tighnari's master, Sir Naphis, called him and Collei to the Akademiya to help out on a project. They should be at Naphis's office at this hour.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Though I must say, I'm surprised you're extending the invitation to Tighnari... Did you do something to offend Sir Naphis?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Don't be outrageous. Naphis offends me all the time — it's never the other way round.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: #Anyway, hurry up and fetch Tighnari. I'll head over to the tavern with {NICKNAME} and Paimon. See you there.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Go on, now. Don't keep us waiting.

talks.objective: Go to the 2nd floor of Lambad's Tavern

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Not to brag, but we never had problems like this at Rtawahist back when I was still teaching... And if you don't want to take my word for it, you can ask them.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: They were students at the time, they'll tell you what it was like. Won't they?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I was out in the forest at least four days a week back then, thanks to a colossal workload from Master. It wrought havoc on my poor tail... So, I didn't exactly keep up to date with what was going on at the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Most of what I know, I heard from Cyno after the fact.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Professor's become a lot more laid-back in his retirement. He used to be far stricter, and was especially known for being extremely principled.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Wow... It's hard enough to stay true to your principles as a normal person. I can't imagine doing that as a sage...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: It's a pity Collei wasn't around at the time... I would have happily taken her on as a student.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: And then we'd have one more person who has to address Lisa as "upperclasswoman"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Can't you just call her "Lisa"...? She seems to prefer it when people treat her like an older sister.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Oh, believe me... Back when she was a student, nothing made her happier than the younger students acknowledging her seniority.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! More food! Are you sure about this? We don't wanna take advantage...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Hahaha, don't worry about it! Order whatever you like, and if it's not enough, order some more! After all your help today, treating you to dinner is the least I can do.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I thought I heard some familiar voices. Ah, and Sir Cyrus is here as well...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Oh, Kaveh! It's been a while. Zaha Hadi was talking about you last month. How have you been?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I've been alright, thank you. You're looking very well, Sir. I'm glad to see it.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Have you eaten yet? Care to join us?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: That's awfully kind of you, but I had a late lunch, so I'm not really hungry just yet. I'll have dinner a little bit later tonight.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I just came to Lambad's to buy some wine, and when I heard some voices I recognized, I thought I'd come and say hello.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: So what's the occasion, anyway? Some sort of celebration?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Ugh, consolation, more like... You wouldn't believe the day I've had...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Cyrus vividly recounts the day's events for the benefit of those who weren't there to witness it...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...Sounds like things have really gone downhill since I was there. In my whole time as a student, I've never heard of anything remotely like that.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I can't believe how young the guy is... *sigh* What are his parents going to think?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Young people are always more susceptible to making rash and ill-advised decisions. Their minds are still developing. It's just an unfortunate fact of life.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: But still! This boy has some nerve, just look at what he wrote! It makes my blood boil!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Wow, yeah... Geez...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: "I will always be watching you and all of your secrets..." And then he just followed you into the House of Daena?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: If this were my son, oh, he'd get the scolding of a lifetime! Hmph!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Luckily, I'm also an extremely principled person.

dialogues.speaker: Lambad
dialogues.text: Kaveh! Your order's ready, Sir!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Ah, coming!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I'll have to get going. Have a nice evening, everyone — I'll catch you all another time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, bye-bye!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Here I am. The coffee beans are in here too?

dialogues.speaker: Lambad
dialogues.text: Yep, it's all there.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: I'll stop babbling away now. Let's eat before the food gets cold.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You were all busy chatting that you almost forgot about the food.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Luckily, it's still hot, and you enjoy a delicious celebratory meal after a crazy day.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Phew...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Too tasty... Paimon's belly is about to explode...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Haha, mine too. I'll have to walk home to burn some of it off.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Thanks for dinner, Sir Cyrus! Master Tighnari and I will bring you some home-made herbal tea next time. It'll do wonders for your sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Well, I look forward to that! In fact, could I trouble you to bring a little extra, for the other old folks on my street? I'll be the envy of the neighborhood!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: No problem at all. I'll pack some up and bring it over.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you for treating us!

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Ah. I'll see you all later! I'd better head home now and tend to the crops.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Good night, Professor. Don't let those tomatoes keep you up too late.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Hey! My tomatoes are serious business! I am not about to be beaten by Zaha Hadi!

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Anyway, I'll be leaving now. Don't stay up too late now, children. I bid you all a good night.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Take care! Have a safe trip home!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Alright. Now, we finally have some "us time."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you mean, "us time"?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Well, I was talking with Tighnari and Collei, and since we all have some free time, we thought we could all go camping together. Think of it as our way of welcoming you back to Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Camping!? That sounds fun, Paimon's in!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Right? It's been so long since we did something fun together. I can't wait!

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Everyone, let's meet tomorrow afternoon at the riverbank to the southeast of Gandharva Ville.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: No need to bring anything — we've already packed everything for the trip. Just bring your delightful selves and prepare to have some fun.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You got it! We'll be there!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Great. Then we'll see you tomorrow.

choices.text: Time to show off my tent-pitching skills!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Wait, no, that's my job! Don't take it away from me... Why don't you and Paimon help out Master, or Cyno?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: You don't have to play the hero when you're out with us! This is your chance to just... y'know, laze around and switch off for a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We haven't seen our Sumeru friends for a while now. Paimon wonders how they're doing...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, let's go to Sumeru City and catch up with them!
